summary: Anas reports that the Prophet said sitting in dhikr from Asr until evening is better than freeing eight slaves from the progeny of Ismaa'eel.
The Prophet said he prefers sitting with people engaged in Allaah's dhikr between Fajr and sunrise to everything the sun rises upon.
notes: No narrator is named in this item.

summary: Sahal bin Sa'd reports that the Prophet said he would rather attend Fajr and then sit in dhikr until sunrise than provide thoroughbred horses for the path of Allaah.
Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib reports that the Prophet said sitting in dhikr from Fajr until sunrise is preferred to freeing four slaves.
The Prophet said he prefers praying Fajr and then sitting in Allaah's dhikr until sunrise over racing a horse in the path of Allaah until sunrise.
notes: Introduced by 'Another narration' with no narrator named.

summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet said he prefers reciting Subhaanallaah, Al Hamdulillaah, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah and Allaahu Akbar over everything the sun rises upon.

Abu Umaamah reports two versions of the Prophet preferring the reciting of the four phrases of dhikr to freeing slaves from the progeny of Ismaa'eel, one version counting two slaves and the other four.
notes: Two separate reports in one item, joined by 'Anotehr narration' (OCR for 'Another narration'); could be split.

summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says he prefers engaging in Allaah's dhikr from morning to night over providing thoroughbred horses for jihaad from morning to night.
notes: OCR reads 'Aliaah' for Allaah in the text.

summary: Abu Ubaydah bin Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says it was difficult for Abdullaah bin Mas'ood to say anything other than the dhikr of Allaah.

people.name: Abu Ubaydah bin Abdullaah bin Mas'ood

notes: Not matched to approved abu-ubaydah-bin-masood, whose name differs here; check whether it is the same person. Sahabi status unconfirmed.

summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood disliked talk between dawn and Fajr and, after Fajr, told people chatting in the masjid either to pray or to stay silent.
notes: Several narrations joined by 'Another narration' and 'Yet another narration'.

summary: Abu Dardaa says he loves saying Allaahu Akbar a hundred times more than giving a hundred gold coins in charity, and Mu'aadh bin Jabal says he prefers dhikr from morning to night over providing horses for jihaad.
notes: Two separate sayings, by Abu Dardaa and by Mu'aadh bin Jabal.

summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that on a journey Abu Moosa Ash'ari stopped people's idle talk and urged him to remember their Rabb.
notes: Ends with an editorial cross-reference ('the rest of the narration has passed in the chapter on Imaan in the Aakhirah'), which is not part of the narration.

summary: Mu'aadh bin Abdullaah bin Raafi reports a gathering where Abdullaah bin Abu Umayrah relayed Mu'aadh bin Jabal's report that the Prophet said one of two phrases rises to the Throne and the other fills the space between heaven and earth, and Abdullaah bin Umar wept on hearing it.
notes: Two narrator names (Mu'aadh bin Abdullaah bin Raafi, Abdullaah bin Abu Umayrah) are not in the approved list.

summary: Jareeri reports that when Anas entered Ihraam from Dhaatul Irq he spoke nothing but the dhikr of Allaah until he came out of Ihraam.
notes: 'Jareeri' is given only as a nisba; not matched to jareer-bin-abdillaah.

summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri narrates that on the Day of Qiyaamah Allaah will say the people of this assembly will soon learn who the people of honour are, and the Prophet said they are those who take part in gatherings of dhikr.
notes: OCR garbles the salutation after the Prophet's name ('(Mi').

summary: Umar narrates that the Prophet said people who attend Fajr and then stay in dhikr until sunrise return sooner, with greater reward, than an expedition that had just come back from Najd with booty.
notes: The text is cut off mid-sentence ('than those of the').

summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Sahl bin Hunayf narrates that when the verse of Surah Kahf 28 was revealed the Prophet went out to find people engaged in dhikr, sat with them, and praised Allaah for placing such people among his Ummah.

people.name: Abdur Rahmaan bin Sahl bin Hunayf

notes: The approved list has abdur-rahmaan-bin-sahl (yes), which may be the same person; not assigned because the names are not certainly the same. OCR cut the verse quotation short ('verse-.').

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas narrates that the Prophet passed Abdullaah bin Rawaaha while he was advising companions, recited Surah Kahf 28 to them, and said that angels say the same dhikr as those gathered and that Allaah forgives them.

Thaabit Bunaani narrates that when the Prophet passed a group engaged in dhikr that included Salmaan, he told them to continue and said Allaah's mercy was descending on them so he wished to join them.

Jaabir reports that the Prophet said angels attend gatherings of dhikr, that such gatherings are the gardens of Jannah, and that Allaah treats a servant according to the esteem in which the servant holds Him.
Jaabir bin Samurah reports that after the Fajr salaah the Prophet used to sit engaged in dhikr until sunrise.
Abdullaah bin Amr asked the Prophet what the reward for gatherings of dhikr would be, and he replied that it is Jannah.
Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says gatherings of dhikr are the life of knowledge and create humility in the heart.

Aa'isha asked the Prophet what he said after every gathering and salaah, and he explained that the words seal the good that was said and expiate the bad; Abu Barzah reports that the Prophet recited them at the end of every gathering.
notes: Two reports (Aa'isha and Abu Barzah) joined, with an unnamed questioner.

summary: A longer version of the du'aa said at the end of a gathering, adding a request for forgiveness for having sinned and wronged oneself, because none but Allaah forgives sins.
notes: Continues the du'aa of n02984; the Prophet is not named in this item (the heading attributes it to him).

summary: Zubayr bin Awwaam reports that the Companions said they fall into talk of the Period of Ignorance after gatherings, and the Prophet advised reciting the du'aa at the end of a gathering to atone for what was said in it.
Abdullaah bin Amr says that certain words, recited three times after any gathering, atone for wrong said in it and seal it, as a letter is sealed.
notes: Gives the same words as n02984 without repeating them; the Prophet is not named.

summary: Abu Dharr asked the Prophet for advice and was told to hold fast to taqwa, and then to be particular about reciting the Qur'aan, which is a light for him on earth and a treasure in the heavens.

Aws bin Hudhayfah describes the Thaqeef delegation's stay in Madinah, when the Prophet came to them late one night because he had not finished his daily portion of the Qur'aan, and his companions explained how he divided the Qur'aan into seven portions.
Mughiera bin Shu'ba narrates that when a man asked to see the Prophet between Makkah and Madinah, the Prophet delayed granting permission because he had not finished his daily portion of the Qur'aan.
Abu Salamah reports that when Umar asked Abu Moosa Ash'ari to remind them of their Rabb, Abu Moosa would begin reciting the Qur'aan.
notes: Only 'Abu Salamah' is given. The approved list has two Abu Salamahs (abu-salma and abu-salma-bin-abdir-rahmaan), so no id was assigned.

summary: Reports of Umar's love for Qur'aan recitation: Abu Moosa Ash'ari recited beautifully when Umar asked him to remind them of their Rabb, and when told it was time for salaah Umar said they were already in salaah; Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Umar would open the Qur'aan and recite when he entered his house.
notes: Three or four separate reports joined. The last report is cut off ('and recite').

summary: Uthmaan says he does not like a single day or night to pass without looking into the Qur'aan and reciting it.
notes: OCR garbled the text ('I notlike', 'i,e.'); the meaning is taken from the parallel narrations n02994 and n02995.

summary: Uthmaan says that had our hearts been pure we would never get enough of the speech of Allaah.

Hasan reports Uthmaan's saying that had hearts been pure they would never tire of Allaah's speech, that he never let a day pass without looking into the Qur'aan, and that the pages of his Qur'aan were worn out by the time of his death.
notes: 'Hadhrat Hasan' is matched to hasan-bin-abil-hasan on the assumption that this is Hasan al-Basri; please confirm.

summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says to always look into the Qur'aan while reciting, because it makes contemplation easier.
notes: The heading names Ibn Umar and Ikrama, but the text is only Ibn Mas'ood's saying.

summary: Habeeb bin Shaheed narrates, through Naafi, that Abdullaah bin Umar made wudu for every salaah and recited Qur'aan between salaahs; Ibn Abu Mulaykah reports that Ikrama bin Abu Jahal placed the Qur'aan on his face and wept.
notes: Two separate reports joined. Stray OCR debris after the first report.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar says that each letter of the Qur'aan recited brings ten good deeds, and that each salutation sent upon the Prophet also brings ten rewards; a second version explains that Alif, Laam and Meem each count for ten rather than the three letters together.
notes: Two versions of the same saying in one item.

summary: Uqba bin Aamir narrates that the Prophet advised him to keep ties with those who sever them, give to those who deprive him and forgive those who wrong him, and then taught him to recite Surahs Ikhlaas, Falaq and Naas every night.
notes: OCR garbles the names of the three Surahs ('CU-i ilii', 'ji)(').

summary: Aa'isha reports that when the Prophet lay down to sleep he blew into his palms after reciting Surahs Ikhlaas and Falaq, then wiped over his body, and that when his illness intensified he asked her to do this for him.
notes: Two versions of the same practice (Ikhlaas and Falaq; then with Naas) joined by 'According to another narration'.
